title: Second-order logic: relation variables and full semantics
summary: Quantify over relations as well as elements, and express the well-order property and all-subset induction in single formulas.
abstract: To say that an order is a well-order, we must consider every nonempty subset and ask whether it has a least element. First-order quantifiers choose elements; second-order quantifiers can choose subsets and relations. We define this enlarged language and explain what it means to let a relation variable range over all relations on a fixed domain. This gives a single formula for the well-order property and a single sentence saying that every successor-closed subset containing zero is the whole domain. We also show how functions can be described by their graphs, and why truth depends only on the free variables.
